items.q: The prize-winning novel was ______ for the stage in 2019, with the narrator's fading memories performed by a chorus.
items.vi: Cuốn tiểu thuyết đoạt giải được chuyển thể cho sân khấu năm 2019, với những ký ức phai nhạt của người kể chuyện do một dàn đồng ca thể hiện.
items.explanation: Adapted for the stage / screen = rewritten in a new artistic form; the clue is for the stage plus memories being performed. ✗ adjusted — a small tweak or correction (adjust the volume), not a re-creation; ✗ converted — changed in use, units or belief (convert a barn, convert to metric), not an artistic reworking; ✗ altered — a vague general change; 'altered for the stage' is not the collocation.

items.q: Most of the mayor's promises about a second airport proved to be ______: no site was ever even surveyed.
items.vi: Phần lớn lời hứa của thị trưởng về sân bay thứ hai hóa ra chỉ là lời nói suông: chưa từng có địa điểm nào được khảo sát.
items.explanation: Hot air = empty talk with nothing behind it; the clue is no site was ever even surveyed. ✗ cold comfort — poor consolation after a loss; ✗ thin ice — a risky, dangerous position (be on thin ice); ✗ sour grapes — pretending not to want what you cannot have.

items.q: Two decades of touring had ______ a heavy toll on the conductor's hearing.
items.vi: Hai thập kỷ lưu diễn đã gây tổn hại nặng nề cho thính giác của vị nhạc trưởng.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is take a (heavy) toll on = cause serious harm, which fits touring … the conductor's hearing. ✗ paid — you pay a toll (a fee) on a road, not on someone's hearing; ✗ made — 'make a toll' is not English; ✗ done — damage is done, but a toll is taken, never done.

items.q: The coach ______ the nine o'clock ferry; it was still in the hotel car park at ten.
items.vi: Chiếc xe khách không thể nào đã kịp chuyến phà chín giờ; mười giờ nó vẫn còn nằm trong bãi đỗ của khách sạn.
items.explanation: A confident deduction that something did not happen uses can't have + past participle; the clue is the evidence still in the car park at ten. ✗ mustn't have caught — in standard exam grammar 'must have' gives only positive deduction; its negative is can't have; ✗ needn't have caught — means it did catch it but did not need to; ✗ shouldn't have caught — criticises something it actually did.

items.q: Researchers found that self-control tends to ______ across the day, sagging after lunch and recovering by early evening.
items.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu nhận thấy khả năng tự chủ có xu hướng dao động trong ngày, sụt xuống sau bữa trưa rồi hồi phục vào đầu buổi tối.
items.explanation: Fluctuate = rise and fall repeatedly, which the clue sagging … recovering describes. ✗ mutate — change into a different (usually genetic) form; ✗ convert — change into a different use or form, and needs 'into'; ✗ transform — change completely into something new, normally with an object; none describes up-and-down movement.

items.q: The campaign to reopen the town's only cinema ______ once its two loudest supporters moved away.
items.vi: Chiến dịch đòi mở lại rạp chiếu phim duy nhất của thị trấn lụi dần rồi tắt hẳn khi hai người ủng hộ nhiệt thành nhất chuyển đi nơi khác.
items.explanation: Fizzle out = end weakly after a promising start; the clue is the campaign losing its two loudest supporters. ✗ wore out — became unusable through use (shoes, patience) or exhausted someone; ✗ broke out — started suddenly (a fire, a war, a rash), the opposite of ending; ✗ passed out — fainted, or handed out (which needs an object).

items.q: ______ had the curtain risen than a phone began ringing in the front row.
items.vi: Màn vừa mới kéo lên thì một chiếc điện thoại đã đổ chuông ngay hàng ghế đầu.
items.explanation: Inverted No sooner had … than: the than later in the sentence decides it. ✗ Hardly — pairs with when (Hardly had the curtain risen when …); ✗ Scarcely — also pairs with when, not than; ✗ Not until — must be followed by a time phrase or clause first (Not until the interval did …), not directly by the inverted main clause.

items.q: Trying to drum up interest in a third sequel after those reviews is ______; the studio would do better to move on.
options: putting the cart before the horse
items.vi: Cố khơi lại sự quan tâm cho phần phim thứ ba sau những bài đánh giá như thế chẳng khác nào phí công vô ích; hãng phim nên chuyển hướng thì hơn.
items.explanation: Flog a dead horse = waste effort on something already finished or hopeless; the clue is the studio would do better to move on. ✗ putting the cart before the horse — doing things in the wrong order; ✗ beating around the bush — avoiding saying something directly; ✗ barking up the wrong tree — pursuing the wrong person or idea, a mistake of target, not of hope.

items.q: Having thrown ______ to the ______, the couple sold their flat and bought one-way tickets to Lisbon.
items.vi: Bất chấp mọi rủi ro, hai vợ chồng bán căn hộ và mua vé một chiều đi Lisbon.
items.explanation: The fixed idiom is throw caution to the wind(s) = stop worrying about risk and act boldly, which sold their flat … one-way tickets shows. ✗ care / winds — the noun in the idiom is caution, not care; ✗ caution / air — the idiom needs wind, not air; ✗ fear / wind — 'throw fear to the wind' is not the expression.

items.q: The curator insisted that every painting on loan ______ insured before it left the building.
items.vi: Người phụ trách bảo tàng nhất quyết yêu cầu mọi bức tranh cho mượn phải được bảo hiểm trước khi rời khỏi tòa nhà.
items.explanation: After insist / demand / recommend that, the verb takes the base-form subjunctive — that every painting be insured — whatever the tense of the main verb. ✗ was — indicative past would report a fact, not a demand; ✗ is — same problem, and clashes with the past 'insisted'; ✗ were — the past subjunctive belongs after 'if / wish' (if it were), not after insist that.

items.q: After the trial of self-service kiosks ended in chaos, the airline ______ to its old check-in desks within a week.
items.vi: Sau khi thử nghiệm quầy tự phục vụ kết thúc trong hỗn loạn, hãng hàng không quay lại dùng quầy làm thủ tục cũ chỉ trong một tuần.
items.explanation: Revert to = go back to a former system or state, matching to its old check-in desks. ✗ reversed — undo or turn round; it needs an object (reverse a decision) and does not take 'to'; ✗ restored — bring back; also needs an object (restore the desks), never 'restore to' a system; ✗ retreated — physical or military withdrawal, not switching systems.

items.q: Good guides learn to ______ a balance between keeping to the timetable and letting the group linger where it wants.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn viên giỏi biết cách giữ được sự cân bằng giữa việc bám sát lịch trình và để đoàn nán lại nơi họ muốn.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is strike a balance = find a fair middle way, confirmed by between … and …. ✗ hit — hit a target or a record, never a balance; ✗ draw — draw a line or a conclusion, not a balance; ✗ set — set a limit or a standard, not a balance.

items.q: After a decade in publishing, she has grown used to ______ manuscripts that are competent but unsellable.
items.vi: Sau một thập kỷ làm xuất bản, cô đã quen với việc từ chối những bản thảo viết ổn nhưng không thể bán được.
items.explanation: After be / get / grow used to, the to is a preposition, so a noun or -ing form follows: used to rejecting. ✗ reject — the bare infinitive follows 'used to' only for a past habit (she used to reject), which 'has grown' rules out; ✗ have rejected — an infinitive form, impossible after a preposition; ✗ being rejected — passive, so it cannot take the object 'manuscripts'; she is the one rejecting.

items.q: The review never calls the play a failure, but anyone able to ______ will sense the critic's disappointment.
items.vi: Bài phê bình không hề gọi vở kịch là thất bại, nhưng ai biết đọc ý tứ ẩn sau câu chữ sẽ cảm nhận được nỗi thất vọng của nhà phê bình.
items.explanation: Read between the lines = understand what is implied but not stated; the clue is never calls … but … will sense. ✗ read the fine print — check the small conditions of a contract; ✗ read the riot act — scold someone severely; ✗ read it and weep — a taunt when showing someone a winning result.

items.q: ______ with the sprawling four-hour original, the director's new ninety-minute cut feels almost brisk.
items.vi: So với bản gốc dài lê thê bốn tiếng, bản dựng mới chín mươi phút của đạo diễn tạo cảm giác gần như gọn gàng, nhanh nhẹn.
items.explanation: The new cut is the thing being compared, so the passive participle Compared with is needed; the clue is the subject the director's new cut. ✗ Comparing — active, would make the cut do the comparing (dangling participle); ✗ To compare — an infinitive of purpose, 'in order to compare', which makes no sense here; ✗ Having compared — active and perfect, again wrongly makes the cut the comparer.

items.q: Rather than a few cosmetic changes, the museum's new director wants to ______ the entire visitor experience, from ticketing to the café.
items.vi: Thay vì vài thay đổi bề ngoài, giám đốc mới của bảo tàng muốn cải tổ toàn diện trải nghiệm của khách tham quan, từ khâu bán vé đến quán cà phê.
items.explanation: Overhaul = examine and rebuild something completely; the clue is rather than a few cosmetic changes … the entire experience. ✗ tweak — make a tiny adjustment, exactly the cosmetic change rejected; ✗ amend — make minor corrections to a text or law; ✗ modify — change partly or slightly, not from top to bottom.

items.q: ______ the critics admired the film's ambition, few of them could sit through its four-hour running time.
items.vi: Dù giới phê bình rất ngưỡng mộ tham vọng của bộ phim, ít ai trong số họ ngồi được hết bốn tiếng chiếu.
items.explanation: Much as + clause = 'although … very much', and a full clause (the critics admired) follows the blank. ✗ Despite — a preposition, needs a noun or -ing (despite admiring), not subject + verb; ✗ However — an adverb; it cannot link two clauses with only a comma; ✗ Nonetheless — also an adverb, same comma-splice problem.

items.q: Managers who announce sweeping changes but never ______ soon lose the trust of their staff.
items.vi: Những nhà quản lý tuyên bố cải cách lớn nhưng không bao giờ thực hiện đến nơi đến chốn sẽ sớm đánh mất lòng tin của nhân viên.
items.explanation: Follow through = complete what you have started or promised; the clue is announce sweeping changes but never …. ✗ follow suit — copy what others have just done; ✗ fall through — (of a plan) collapse; managers cannot 'fall through'; ✗ carry out — perform, but it needs an object (carry out the changes) and the blank has none.

items.q: Fans who had queued overnight were ______ disappointed when the author cancelled her signing at the last minute.
items.vi: Những người hâm mộ xếp hàng suốt đêm đã thất vọng cay đắng khi tác giả hủy buổi ký tặng vào phút chót.
items.explanation: Bitterly disappointed is the standard collocation, intensified by queued overnight. ✗ strongly — goes with advise, oppose, recommend, not disappointed; ✗ heavily — goes with rain, traffic, rely, not disappointed; ✗ highly — goes with likely, recommended, successful, not disappointed.

items.q: The interviewer asked the novelist ______ she had ever thought of abandoning the book halfway.
items.vi: Người phỏng vấn hỏi nữ tiểu thuyết gia liệu bà có bao giờ nghĩ đến chuyện bỏ dở cuốn sách giữa chừng không.
items.explanation: A reported yes/no question is introduced by whether (or if) with statement word order; the clue is asked … she had ever. ✗ that — reports a statement, not a question; ✗ did — keeps direct-question order (did she …), which reported speech drops; ✗ how — asks about manner, but the original question was yes/no.

items.q: A seasoned tour guide knows how to ______: if the group is flagging, the lecture on Gothic arches can wait.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn viên dày dạn biết cách nắm bắt tâm trạng đoàn: nếu cả nhóm đã thấm mệt, bài giảng về vòm Gothic có thể để sau.
items.explanation: Read the room = sense the mood of the people present and adjust; the clue is if the group is flagging … can wait. ✗ call the shots — be the one in charge; ✗ hold the floor — keep speaking while others listen, the opposite of pausing the lecture; ✗ steal the show — attract all the attention.

items.q: The two novelists reviewed ______ books for thirty years without once meeting in person.
items.vi: Hai nhà tiểu thuyết đã bình sách của nhau suốt ba mươi năm mà chưa từng một lần gặp mặt.
items.explanation: A possessive is needed before the noun books, so each other's = the other's books. ✗ each other — an object pronoun, cannot modify a noun; ✗ one another — same problem, no 's; ✗ themselves — reflexive, would mean each reviewed his own books, which contradicts 'without once meeting'.

items.q: Before the festival put the town on the map, most families ______ by ______ fishing and a little farming.
items.vi: Trước khi lễ hội khiến thị trấn nổi tiếng, hầu hết các gia đình sống qua ngày nhờ đánh cá và làm nông chút ít.
items.explanation: Get by on something = survive using only that (get by on a small income), matching fishing and a little farming. ✗ went / on — 'go by' means pass (the years went by), not survive; ✗ made / on — 'make by' is not a phrasal verb; ✗ got / from — get by takes on for the means, not from.

items.q: Her editor asked her to ______ the manuscript one last time, cutting the second act and sharpening the dialogue.
items.vi: Biên tập viên đề nghị cô sửa lại bản thảo lần cuối, cắt bỏ hồi hai và làm cho lời thoại sắc sảo hơn.
items.explanation: Revise = rework and improve a text; the clue is cutting the second act and sharpening the dialogue. ✗ reverse — turn round or undo (reverse a decision); ✗ rectify — correct a specific error or fault, not reshape a whole manuscript; ✗ revert — go back to an earlier state, and takes 'to', not an object.

items.q: Nobody on the coach tour actually read the itinerary before setting off, ______?
items.vi: Chẳng ai trên chuyến xe du lịch thực sự đọc lịch trình trước khi khởi hành, phải không?
items.explanation: Nobody makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive; nobody takes the pronoun they, and simple past read needs did. ✗ didn't they — a negative tag after an already-negative statement; ✗ did he — 'nobody' takes they, not he; ✗ had they — 'had' needs past perfect, but 'read' here is simple past (no 'had' before it).
